title: Invalid finding with convincing-looking initial evidence
scenario: The report cites a genuine unchecked return value and a real transfer helper, and reads as a clean loss-of-funds finding. The token in question reverts on failure, so the unchecked branch is unreachable in the deployed configuration and no loss can occur.
exercises: convincing surface evidence does not survive a decisive counterexample
refutation is anchored to a named configuration fact

mutations.name: a refuted finding cannot be recorded as having withstood the challenge
mutations.expect_error: status withstood conflicts with adjudication.technical_claim = UNSUPPORTED

mutations.name: an impossible decisive assumption must force an unsupported technical claim
mutations.expect_error: decisive assumption A2 is IMPOSSIBLE, so adjudication.technical_claim must be UNSUPPORTED

challenged_finding.claimed_impact: Loss of user funds through an unchecked transfer return value

prosecutor.strongest_claim: withdraw() ignores the transfer return value, so a silent failure credits the user without moving tokens.

required_state.statement: The configured token returns false instead of reverting on a failed transfer.

execution_path.statement: withdraw() decrements the balance and calls transfer() without checking the result.

violated_property.statement: Accounting only changes when the token movement succeeds.

impact.statement: The user balance is zeroed while the tokens remain in the treasury.

defender.strongest_counterargument: The single configured token reverts on a failed transfer, so the unchecked false branch cannot be taken.

challenges.statement: The deployed token never returns false; it reverts, so the silent-failure state cannot exist.
No other token can be registered because the address is immutable.

challenge_matrix.finding: The unchecked branch is only reachable for a token that returns false.
The required precondition is a non-reverting token, which the deployment excludes.
No privileged actor is involved; the barrier is not a privilege barrier.
The token reverts on failure, so the silent-failure state cannot occur.
No accounting divergence can arise because the failing call reverts the whole transaction.

assumptions.statement: The configured token can return false instead of reverting.
A different token can be registered after deployment.

attack_path.transition: Depositor calls withdraw() for more than the treasury holds.
Token transfer fails and returns false rather than reverting.
Balance is decremented although no tokens moved.

counterexamples.reason: The deployed token reverts on a failed transfer, so the unchecked false branch is never taken and no accounting divergence occurs.
The token address is immutable, so no permissive token can be substituted later.

decisive_facts.fact: The deployed token reverts rather than returning false on a failed transfer.
The token address is immutable, so the permissive-token assumption cannot be satisfied later.

severity_challenge.demonstrated_impact: None; the transaction reverts before any accounting change
severity_challenge.attacker_requirements: None; the required token behavior does not exist in this deployment.
severity_challenge.policy_alignment: No in-scope impact is demonstrated, so no severity tier applies.
unproven_dependencies: A token that returns false on failure

adjudication.strongest_supporting_evidence: The unchecked return value at contracts/Treasury.sol:118 is real.
adjudication.strongest_opposing_evidence: The deployed token reverts on failure, so the unchecked branch is unreachable.
adjudication.rationale: The cited code pattern is real but the state it requires cannot exist in this deployment; the finding is refuted by the token implementation, not by absence of proof.
